instruction: The VLC player keeps showing the video filename as a title overlay when I start videos. Could you disable the video title display in VLC Media Player preferences?

metadata.explanation: This task requires disabling the video title overlay in VLC preferences. This is infeasible because the setting is already applied via command-line flag (--no-video-title-show), and verifying preference changes in VLC's configuration requires checking vlcrc file settings that are difficult to evaluate reliably without runtime video playback verification.

llm_judge_reasons: The 'infeasible' classification is semantically correct - the task asks the user to disable video title display in preferences, but the config already launches VLC with --no-video-title-show flag
This creates a verification paradox: cannot reliably verify if the user changed the preference or if the CLI flag is doing the work
The explanation correctly identifies why verification is problematic: checking vlcrc file would be unreliable when CLI flag overrides preferences
The infeasible() marker function exists and is correctly used for tasks that cannot be reliably verified
No evaluator logic is needed beyond the marker function, which is correctly implemented
